**Title (English, from literature):** Borrowing a robe

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cīvarasaṅkamanīya* is the twenty-fifth expiation rule (*pācittiya*) in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* of the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule lays down that a nun who wears a borrowed robe without the permission of its owner commits an offense requiring confession. An English translation of the text has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Within the Pali Vinaya, it corresponds to *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* Pācittiya 25 and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* Pācittiya 25. Cross-tradition parallels exist in Chinese translation in the Dharmaguptaka vinaya (*Bi Vb* Pc 106 and *Bi Pm* Pc 106) and the Mahāsāṃghika vinaya (*Bi Vb* Pc 71 and *Bi Pm* Pc 71), as well as in Sanskrit in the Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅga* (Pc 71). In addition, computational analysis by DharmaNexus detects 383 internal Pali matches across 98 texts, reflecting standard Vinaya legal formulae shared with other rules in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (notably Bi-Vb Pc 18, Pc 6, Pc 23, and Pc 19) and the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (such as Bu-Vb Pc 2), while yielding no cross-language matches meeting the threshold score [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
